title: Left-coefficient action laws from normalized open restriction
statement:
Use monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with associator $\alpha:(U\otimes V)\otimes W\to U\otimes(V\otimes W)$ and left unitor $\lambda$. A strong monoidal functor has the structure of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]; write $\delta^H_{U,V}:H(U\otimes V)\xrightarrow{\sim}HU\otimes HV$ and $e_H:H\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1$ for its inverse structure maps. Set $h^H_N=\lambda_N\circ(e_H\otimes1_N)$ and $a^H_{B,B',N}=\alpha_{HB,HB',N}\circ(\delta^H_{B,B'}\otimes1_N)$. Composition is right to left.
A symmetry $\beta_{U,V}:U\otimes V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\otimes U$ means natural involutive tensor swaps satisfying the hexagon identities with $\alpha$; a symmetric strong monoidal functor preserves these swaps under $\delta$.
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be symmetric monoidal categories, $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a symmetric strong monoidal functor, and $J:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ a fully faithful left adjoint to $Q$. Here fully faithful means that $J$ induces bijections on all Hom sets. Let $u:1_{\mathcal D}\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$ be the adjunction unit, using the convention of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Suppose given natural isomorphisms $\gamma_{M,C}:JM\otimes C\xrightarrow{\sim}J(M\otimes QC)$ for all $M\in\mathcal D$, $C\in\mathcal C$, with the specified restriction normalization
$$u_{M\otimes QC}^{-1}\circ Q(\gamma_{M,C})=(u_M^{-1}\otimes1_{QC})\circ\delta^Q_{JM,C}.$$
Define $v_{C,M}=J(\beta_{M,QC})\circ\gamma_{M,C}\circ\beta_{C,JM}:C\otimes JM\xrightarrow{\sim}J(QC\otimes M)$. Then $v$ is natural, has the left-coefficient normalization
$$u_{QC\otimes M}^{-1}\circ Q(v_{C,M})=(1_{QC}\otimes u_M^{-1})\circ\delta^Q_{C,JM},$$
and satisfies, for every $C,C'\in\mathcal C$, $M\in\mathcal D$,
$$J(h^Q_M)\circ v_{\mathbf1,M}=\lambda_{JM},$$
$$J(a^Q_{C,C',M})\circ v_{C\otimes C',M}=v_{C,QC'\otimes M}\circ(1_C\otimes v_{C',M})\circ\alpha_{C,C',JM}.$$
These are equalities in $\mathcal C$ for the specified $\gamma$, not assertions that arbitrary isomorphisms with these sources and targets satisfy the laws.
